questions.question: Explain how a liquid thermometer works and how to read it.
questions.expected_answer: When the air warms, the liquid in the thin tube expands and rises, and when the air cools, it contracts and falls. A scale shows the temperature in degrees Celsius. To read it, look at the top of the liquid with your eye level with it and read the nearest mark, without holding the bulb.

questions.question: Why is a thermometer kept in a Stevenson screen?
questions.expected_answer: Air temperature must be measured in the shade. The white box reflects the sun's heat, its slatted sides let air flow through while keeping out sunlight and rain, and its legs hold the thermometer about one and a half metres above the hot ground, in an open place away from walls.

questions.question: Describe how to measure rainfall correctly.
questions.expected_answer: Use a rain gauge, which measures rain in millimetres. Place it in an open place, away from trees, roofs and walls, with its top level. Read it at the same time every day and then empty it. Add up the daily readings to get weekly, monthly or yearly totals.
